section_summary: This section continues a report on Japan’s April 1947 elections, held before the new Constitution took effect. It explains the significance of the national and local contests, the election schedule and procedures, changes to election law, expanded voting rights, and the screening of candidates under the purge ordinances.

subfiles.title: Report on the April 1947 Elections in Japan
subfiles.about: The significance, administration, legal safeguards, and candidate screening for Japan’s April 1947 elections.
subfiles.summary: The report describes the first elections under Japan’s new constitutional and local government arrangements, including the contests for both Diet houses, local executives, and local assemblies. It explains how the elections were scheduled around the Constitution’s commencement and the purge, and recounts a Diet dispute over amendments to the House of Representatives Election Law. It then details voting and counting procedures, campaign limits, expanded suffrage for women and repatriates, and the screening required of candidates and election officials. The section ends with a table of candidacies, questionnaires, and offices.
